translationRepairs: Tang Jian, whose courtesy name was Maoyue, came from Jinyang in Bing Province. He was the grandson of Yin, who had served Northern Qi as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
Tang Jian, whose courtesy name was Maoyue, came from Jinyang in Bing Province. He was the grandson of Yin, who had served Northern Qi as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
尚書左僕射 is the Left Pushe of the Shangshu (Department of State Affairs), not the Imperial Secretariat (中書).
While Gaozu held Taiyuan as deputy, Jian grew close to Taizong and, in easy conversation, urged him that the Sui court had lost its way and that the realm might be seized.
While Gaozu was garrison commander at Taiyuan, Jian grew close to Taizong and, in easy conversation, urged him that the Sui court had lost its way and that the realm might be seized.
留守 here is the Taiyuan garrison/regency post, not a generic 'deputy'.
In Wude 1 he became Secretariat Drafter, was soon promoted Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was specially granted the additional rank of Formation Attendant.
In Wude 1 he became Secretariat Drafter, was soon promoted Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was specially granted the additional rank of Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary.
散騎常侍 is the cavalier attendant title, not 'Formation Attendant'.

When he returned from duty abroad he became Minister of Rites and Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Strategies Office, while also serving as Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat; he was enfeoffed Duke of Ju, granted with the other founding meritocrats a single pardoned capital offense, appointed military governor of Suizhou with six hundred fief households in Mian Prefecture, and honored with a portrait in the Lingyan Pavilion.

When he returned from duty abroad he became Minister of Rites and Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Strategies Office, while also serving as Acting Vice Director of the Chancellery (Yellow Gate); he was enfeoffed Duke of Ju, granted with the other founding meritocrats a single pardoned capital offense, appointed military governor of Suizhou with six hundred fief households in Mian Prefecture, and honored with a portrait in the Lingyan Pavilion.
檢校黃門侍郎 is the Chancellery/Yellow Gate vice directorship, not the Secretariat (中書).
Zhangsun Shunde, Zhangsun Shunde, was a clansman uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.
Zhangsun Shunde was a clansman uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.
Literal English repeats the personal name; Chinese has a single occurrence of Zhangsun Shunde.
His father Kai had held a Sui palace guard command.
His father Kai had held the Sui honorific rank of kaifu.
Kaifu is an honorific permitting an official headquarters, not a palace-guard command.
His father Kai was a Sui Palace Guard commander.
His father Kai was a Sui kaifu.
Literal invents a palace-guard post for kaifu.
When Gaozu ascended the throne, Shunde was made General of the Left Martial Tiger Guards and enfeoffed Duke of Xue.
When Gaozu ascended the throne, Shunde was made General-in-Chief of the Left Courageous Guards and enfeoffed Duke of Xue.
Zuo Xiaowei is the Courageous Guard, not the tiger-guard title.
In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again granted Honored Equal to the Three Excellencies of the Palace Office.
In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again granted Honored Equal to the Three Excellencies.
Kaifu yitong sansi does not mention a Palace Office.
Liu Hongji, Liu Hongji, was a native of Chiyang in Yong Prefecture.
Liu Hongji was a native of Chiyang in Yong Prefecture.
Literal repeats the personal name; Chinese opens once with Liu Hongji.

Taizong, stricken with illness, halted at Gaogai City. Hongji, Liu Wenjing, and others fought Ju at Qianshui Plain, but the imperial forces fared badly and all eight commanders-in-chief were defeated;

Taizong, stricken with illness, halted at Gaozhi City. Hongji, Liu Wenjing, and others fought Ju at Qianshui Plain, but the imperial forces fared badly and all eight commanders-in-chief were defeated;
Chinese 高墌城 is Gaozhi, not Gaogai.
He followed Taizong to Baiyu, led two thousand men from Xi Prefecture toward Xihe, and cut the rebels' line of retreat.
He followed Taizong to Baibi, led two thousand men from Xi Prefecture toward Xihe, and cut the rebels' line of retreat.
Chinese 柏壁 is Baibi, not Baiyu.

Gaozong mourned him with a three-day suspension of court, posthumously made him Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Bangle and Area Commander of Bing Prefecture, had him buried at Zhaoling with a commemorative stele, and granted the posthumous name Xiang.

Gaozong mourned him with a three-day suspension of court, posthumously made him Commander Unequaled in Honor and Area Commander of Bing Prefecture, had him buried at Zhaoling with a commemorative stele, and granted the posthumous name Xiang.
開府儀同三司 is not Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Bangle.
He joined the campaign against Xue Ju as army supervisor on the grand marshal's staff.
He joined the campaign against Xue Ju as adjutant (sima) on the grand marshal's staff.
元帥府司馬 is headquarters sima/adjutant, not army supervisor.
In Wude 2 he concurrently served as Minister of War on the Shandong Grand Commissioner staff and was then transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
In Wude 2 he concurrently served as Minister of War on the Shan-east Grand Commissioner staff and was then transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
陝東道 is east of Shan, not Shandong 山東.
Taizong came in person to mourn him and wept bitterly, posthumously making him Right Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Grand Commissioner and granting the posthumous name Jie.
Taizong came in person to mourn him and wept bitterly, posthumously making him Right Vice Commissioner of the Shan-east Grand Commissioner and granting the posthumous name Jie.
陝東 is Shan-east, not Shandong.
In the second year of Wude he concurrently served as Minister of War of the Grand Commissioner of the Shandong circuit and was transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
In the second year of Wude he concurrently served as Minister of War of the Grand Commissioner of the Shan-east circuit and was transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
Literal English also renders 陝東 as Shandong.
Qiao's younger clansman Wenli was a man of letters who served as crown prince attendant in the Wude era, began compiling the History of Liang, and died before finishing it.
Qiao's younger second cousin Wenli was a man of letters who, in the Wude era, served as Secretary in the Crown Prince's household, began compiling the History of Liang, and died before finishing it.
從祖弟 is a patrilineal second-cousin, not a vague clansman, and 太子中舍人 is a named secretariat post in the heir's household rather than a generic attendant.
His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was made Duke of Yu, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed commandant of the emperor's sons-in-law.
His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yu, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed commandant of the emperor's sons-in-law.
改封 marks a change of fief, which the idiomatic rendering flattens to a first grant; the literal already preserves re-enfeoffment.
Jiancheng and Yuanji were traveling from Hedong when they met Shao on the road. Jiancheng confided to him, "The summons to return is urgent—I fear Father has already risen in arms.
Jiancheng and Yuanji were traveling from Hedong when they met Shao on the road. Jiancheng confided to him, "The summons to return is urgent—I fear the uprising has already begun.
The Chinese 恐已起事 does not name the father; the idiomatic English invents Father as the subject of the uprising.
He was appointed chief clerk of the Right Army Aide Staff of the Grand Army Commander.
He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Right Leading Army Grand Area Command.
右領軍大都督府長史 is chief clerk of the Right Leading Army grand commandery, not an Army Aide Staff.
In Xianqing 1, as the empress's father, he was posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed Duke of Zhou.
In Xianqing 1, as the empress's father, he was posthumously advanced to Situ (Minister of Education) and re-enfeoffed Duke of Zhou.
Chinese 司徒 is Situ, not Grand Tutor (太傅). The idiomatic rendering invents the wrong office.
In the first year of Xianqing, as empress's father he was posthumously advanced in succession to Grand Tutor and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Zhou.
In the first year of Xianqing, as the empress's father he was posthumously advanced in succession to Situ and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Zhou.
Literal English also mistranslates 司徒 as Grand Tutor.

Wu Shiyi—the second elder brother Shiyi. He too had battle merit. At the beginning of Wude he served as household section chief in the Prince of Qi's mansion and was granted the title Duke of Anlu County.

Wu Shiyi. Shiyi's second elder brother Shiyi also had battle merit. At the beginning of Wude he served as household section chief in the Prince of Qi's mansion and was granted the title Duke of Anlu County.
The heading 武士逸 is a different given name from 士鸊, but the dash fuses them as if one person rather than introducing the second elder brother.
His son Zhewei served as General of the Right Stationing Camp and inherited the title Duke of Qiao.
His son Zhewei served successively as General of the Right Stationing Camp and inherited the title Duke of Qiao.
Chinese 歷 marks successive service; the idiomatic line omits that sense, which the literal already keeps.

Jian's and Guan's own career dates are not stated in owned units.
Empress Wende Shunsheng is named only as Shunde's clanswoman niece; her own dates are not given.
Qiao (嶠) is named only as Wenli's senior clansman; this chunk does not state his own offices or dates.
Yin Kaishan appears only as Zhenghui's later temple companion; owned units do not date Yin's own career.
Silent subject/father of Zhewei is unnamed in owned units; local p001 is a boundary continuation only.
